coredata.dc:description: The comprehensive utilization of wasted pickling sludge in the cement kiln would be a promising practice, but the calcination process of cement clinker became complicated due to the simultaneous introduction of titanium and fluorine. In this paper, the formation and hydration of tricalcium silicate (C3S) doped with CaF2 and TiO2 were discerned by XRD, FT-IR, XPS and isothermal calorimetry. The results revealed that the addition of CaF2 more than 1.5% would promote the appearance of CaTiO3 as the indicator of the solution limit of TiO2, and the formation of CaTiO3 and β-C2S was a concomitant process as the solution limit of TiO2 reached. The addition of 0.5% TiO2 and some addition of CaF2 (≤1.5%) would reduce the polymorph symmetry of C3S, while more addition of CaF2 and TiO2 would actualize the higher polymorph symmetry from M1 to R form. The IR spectra for the polymorphs (T3, M3, R + M3, R) became broader with the increase of the polymorph symmetry of C3S. The replacement of O2− by F− would not be interfered by the simultaneous introduction of titanium, a Ti2p 1/2 peak at 463.39 eV reflected the solution of titanium in the structure of C3S, and the defect reactions of the doped C3S with CaF2 and TiO2 were proposed. The doped C3S had a higher heat flow than the undoped C3S in the initial period, the more addition of CaF2 inhibited the initial hydration activity of C3S, while the addition of TiO2 improved the effect. The incorporation of TiO2 into the doped C3S aggravated the retardation effect caused by CaF2 on the hydration in the acceleration period. The dopant types displayed a more distinct effect than the types of C3S polymorphs on the hydration activity of C3S.

ce:abstract-sec.ce:simple-para: The comprehensive utilization of wasted pickling sludge in the cement kiln would be a promising practice, but the calcination process of cement clinker became complicated due to the simultaneous introduction of titanium and fluorine. In this paper, the formation and hydration of tricalcium silicate (C3S) doped with CaF2 and TiO2 were discerned by XRD, FT-IR, XPS and isothermal calorimetry. The results revealed that the addition of CaF2 more than 1.5% would promote the appearance of CaTiO3 as the indicator of the solution limit of TiO2, and the formation of CaTiO3 and β-C2S was a concomitant process as the solution limit of TiO2 reached. The addition of 0.5% TiO2 and some addition of CaF2 (≤1.5%) would reduce the polymorph symmetry of C3S, while more addition of CaF2 and TiO2 would actualize the higher polymorph symmetry from M1 to R form. The IR spectra for the polymorphs (T3, M3, R + M3, R) became broader with the increase of the polymorph symmetry of C3S. The replacement of O2− by F− would not be interfered by the simultaneous introduction of titanium, a Ti2p 1/2 peak at 463.39 eV reflected the solution of titanium in the structure of C3S, and the defect reactions of the doped C3S with CaF2 and TiO2 were proposed. The doped C3S had a higher heat flow than the undoped C3S in the initial period, the more addition of CaF2 inhibited the initial hydration activity of C3S, while the addition of TiO2 improved the effect. The incorporation of TiO2 into the doped C3S aggravated the retardation effect caused by CaF2 on the hydration in the acceleration period. The dopant types displayed a more distinct effect than the types of C3S polymorphs on the hydration activity of C3S.

ce:section.ce:para: An exponential population growth, a rapid urbanization and a remarkable infrastructure volumes have boosted incrementally the generation of municipal and industrial solid wastes. World Bank Project counted the production of municipal solid waste to reach approximately 2.6 million tons by the end of 2025 [1]. Synchronously, industrial solid wastes such as oil-based mud from oil-well drilling [2], iron ore tailings [3], dam fine sediment from marine dredging operations [4], vitrified medical wastes bottom ash [5], waste gypsum [6], spent catalyst [7], spent activated carbon of potabilization plants [8], and various post-industrial wastes [9] were ceaselessly emerging with great quantities, the contamination issues engendered by disposing these wastes has triggered far-reaching concerns. The global cement production was over 5.0 billion tons in 2018 and still drifting upward [10], it might make the cement industry become a promising alleviation for these disposal issues. The cement kiln co-processing technology has been extensively concerned by many researchers from various countries [11–15], this waste treatment practice is becoming more universal for high reaction temperatures over 1000 °C, long residence times, good turbulence and mixing conditions [16,17]. However, these industrial and municipal wastes generally contained a certain amount of heavy metals and some other impurities, it would shift or degrade the multiple properties of the produced clinker [18,19]. The persuasive investigations and the sufficient researches would be necessary before applying this utilization in practice. To reinforce the rationality and applicability of co-processing different wastes in the cement kiln, a number of explorations about the doping effects by the various elements on the cement clinkers kept unfolding.

Exemplifying the waste pickling sludge generated from the manufacturing of titanium and titanium alloy, and plenty of hydrofluoric acid, as one of the effective pickling solvent, were employed to remove the stains and residual oxide film on the surface of the titanium products [20]. The waste pickling sludge would be generated by a series of technological processes. To realize the proper application of these waste pickling sludge as one part of reutilized resource, co-processing the waste pickling sludges as part of raw meal in cement kiln could be a promising practice. However, the incorporation of the waste pickling sludge into the cement raw meal would result in the increased complexity of calcination progress due to the simultaneous introduction of titanium and fluorine.

CaF2 was recognized as the most experimented mineralizer and flux, it could not only stimulate the cement clinker formation, but also lessen energy consumption during cement clinker sintering [21–22]. For a given clinkering temperature range from 1200 °C to 1450 °C, the addition of fluorite (CaF2) in the raw meal could promote the formation of C3S and improve the burnability and lower clinkering temperatures of oxide melts by 50–100 °C. The solid-state diffusion would be enhanced, the viscosity and surface tension of the liquid-state could be also reduced [21–26]. But it had a slight effect on the decomposition of calcite [27]. The NMR findings expounded that the fluoride anions are preferentially incorporated into the alite structure in substitution of the O2− not linked to silicon [28], and the substitution of free O2− by F− will lead to an excess of positive charge which have to be compensated by as much calcium vacancies [29–30]. Guan et al. [31] demonstrated that one defect reaction would present as fluoride anions were incorporated into the C3S structure:

The results indicated that the pure C3S had the lowest symmetry with a triclinic form T, but the polymorph of C3S doped with 1.0 wt% CaF2 came to be a monoclinic form M1, the polymorph of C3S transformed into rhombohedral form R with 2.0 wt% CaF2 doping [31]. Kacimi et al. [32] revealed that the presence of F− accelerated the formation of alite and altered the original morphology and the crystal size of alite, besides, the high alite content and its disturbed crystal lattice induced by F− introduction could improve the clinker hydraulic reactivity. Emanuelson et al. [33] once pointed that the improved hydraulic activity of mineralised clinker was caused by the introduction of defects with substitutions rather than a change in polymorph symmetry of alite. It was clarified that the decreased hydraulic activity of the mineralised clinker could be attributed to the high levels of fluoride, 0.4 wt% F, it might originate from the formation of insoluble barrier layers on the surface of the clinker minerals. Therefore, to realize the proper performance of resulted clinkers, the maximum incorporation level of fluoride should be approximately 0.25–0.6% (0.5–1.2% CaF2) by weight [26,34–35].

TiO2 in a moderate addition would affect acid based equilibrium [MeO4]5− and [MeO5]9− in the clinker melt to make the viscosity of melt lower and the surface tension higher [18,19]. Both cases could accelerate the assimilation/binding of lime and favor the crystallization of clinkering reactants [19]. Katyal et al [36] once pointed that the introduction of TiO2 could change the polymorphic form of tricalcium silicate differently in different additions: Up to 2.0% TiO2, triclinic form, 4.0–5.0% TiO2, monoclinic form, and 6.0% TiO2, rhombohedral form. It was ascertained that TiO2 would be incorporated into C3S up to 4.5% at 1450 °C and beyond this limit a new phase CaO·TiO2 would form. For hydration process, the presence of small quantity of TiO2 could enhance the hydraulic activity of cement clinker, it could be attributed to the lattice distortion of alite and belite crystal caused by the substitution of the Si4+ ion by Ti4+ ion and the formation of corresponding solid solutions [30]. Katyal et.al [37] also revealed that introduction of TiO2 into C3S affected the hydraulicity of C3S by modifying the polymorphism of C3S and forming a CaO·TiO2 compound. The presence of up to 2.0% TiO2 slowed down the hydration process for about 2 days and then picked up to exceed the degree of hydration of undoped C3S. Higher percentages of TiO2 above 2.0% showed a higher hydration rate from 1 h to 28 d. Shang et al. [38] reported that TiO2-doped could accelerate the hydration activity of clinker in the initial period while postponed the hydration of C3S in the later period, and after hydration of 28 d, C-S-H gel polymerization degree improved by introduction of TiO2 less than 1.5% by mass. Beyond it, the polymerization degree came to reduce.

Though these existing findings have demonstrated the single effect of CaF2 or TiO2 on the formation and hydration performances of clinker minerals, the studies regarding the co-doping effects of CaF2 and TiO2 on the formation of clinker minerals were scare, and its effects on the properties of clinker minerals also need further study. These all are the essential parts to evaluate the feasibility of co-processing the pickling sludge in the cement kiln. Therefore, this study would concentrate on tricalcium silicate (C3S) to identify the formation and hydration of C3S doped with CaF2 and TiO2. The formation of C3S and the polymorphs of C3S were investigated by XRD. The characteristics of IR spectra of C3S doped with CaF2 and TiO2 were discussed. The chemical valence states of fluorine and titanium in the doped C3S was determined by XPS, and the effect of CaF2 and TiO2 on the hydration activity of C3S was explored by isothermal heat flow calorimeter.

The undoped and doped C3S samples were synthesized by a conventional solid-state sintering method. The analytical grade chemical reagents SiO2, CaCO3, CaF2, and TiO2 were regarded as the starting materials. Table 1 provided the detailed compositions of the different doped C3S samples. It should be noted that the redundant calcium from the introduction of CaF2 into the doped C3S samples would interfere the final form of C3S, so the brought calcium by CaF2 should be taken off from the CaCO3 content. The addition of TiO2 would be based on the total mass of CaCO3 and SiO2, and was not affected by the addition of CaF2. The previously dried 1.0 mol SiO2 and 3.0 mol CaCO3 powders with or without the different types and dosages of dopants were homogenized for 3 h in a small-scale powder mixer. The mixtures were then mixed with deionized water again for 0.5 h and pressed into cylindrical pellets at 40.0 MPa. The pellets were sintered in a tubular high temperature furnace XCSL-16–17 V with the successive sintering procedures in Table 2 . The air-quenched sintered samples would be reground to powders, pelletized and sintered using the same sintering procedures until a less than 0.1% (wt. %) free lime content of the sintered samples reached.

The free lime contents of the doped C3S samples were analyzed by the ethanol-glycol method using F Ca-2008 free lime measuring instrument. All the mineral X-ray diffraction of the undoped and doped C3S samples were measured by X-Ray diffraction (XRD, a Bruker D8 Advance) in the 5°–65° (2θ) with CuKα1,2 (λ1 = 0.15406 nm, λ2 = 0.15444 nm) at 40 KV and 40 mA. The procedures of smoothing, background deducting and Kα stripping were implemented on the all raw XRD patterns. The full XRD data was collected over 5°–65° with 0.02° step width and 1.0 s step time. The regional XRD data in the range of 31.5°–33° and 51°–52.5° was rescanned with 0.003° step width and 1.0 s step time.
Bruker Vertex 70 Fourier transform infrared spectrometer was used to measure the FT-IR spectra of some doped C3S samples among the region 400 cm−1–4000 cm−1 at a spectral resolution of 4 cm−1.

X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis was carried out by using a Thermo ESCALAB 250XI photoelectron spectrometer fitted with Mg Kα (hν = 1253.6 eV) X-ray source operating at 16 KV, 14.9 mA. A small portion of the doped C3S samples was ground into fine powders (less than 75 μm) and pressed into a stainless steel sample holder. The pass energies of survey and narrow spectra were 100 eV and 30 eV. The measured data would be extracted from the XPS spectra via a Thermo Avantage Version 5.976 software. A Shirley background was assumed in the all cases. The XPS spectra was corrected for the charging effects by the adventitious carbon peak C1s line at a BE = 284.8 eV. The spectra retrieval was proceeded with built-in XPS Knowledge View in Thermo Avantage software and NIST X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Database (website available: https://srdata.nist.gov/xps/Default.aspx) [39].

The developments of heat flow and total hydration heat of the doped C3S samples were monitored by the TAM Air isothermal calorimetry. The selected samples were ground to pass 75 μm sieve, and the calorimetric measurements were proceeded at 25 °C for 7 d with w/c = 0.5. The samples were well mixed with water and stirred outside the calorimeter using a homemade mixer. The measurement would start 1 min after the mixing procedure.

ce:section.ce:section-title: XRD analysis of doped C3S samples
ce:section.ce:para: The full XRD pattern analysis was carried out to identify the effects of CaF2 and TiO2 on the formation of C3S under the different doping conditions. The results were presented in Fig. 1 (a–m) and Table 3 . The regional XRD patterns in the range of 31.5°–33° and 51°–52.5° were the important fingerprint-regions of the symmetries of different C3S polymorphs [40–42]. The various C3S polymorphs (T1, T2, T3, M1, M3 and R) would be determined by the characteristic peaks referring to the existing researches [41–46]. The built-in illustrations in Fig. 1 (a–m) showed the two selected regions, and the main information of the C3S polymorphs under the different doping conditions were summarized in Table 3.

The phase compositions of different doped C3S samples indicated that the addition of CaF2 from 1.0% to 2.0% would not interfere the formation of C3S phase, but the CaF2 and TiO2 exhibited a distinct effect on the formation of C3S phase. The appearance of CaTiO3 would indicate the solution limit of TiO2 in the doped C3S samples, and the solution limit of TiO2 appeared earlier compared with the Katyal’s findings [36]. The addition of 1.0% CaF2 and 2.0% TiO2 could make the solution limit of TiO2 appear, while the addition of 1.5% or 2.0% CaF2 and 1.0% TiO2 could make the solution limit of TiO2 appear. Hence, the prior solution of CaF2 in the doped C3S would accelerate the appearance of the solution limit of TiO2. It could be observed that the formation of CaTiO3 was accompanied with the formation of β-C2S, it implied the formation reaction of CaTiO3 would assimilate the CaO from the reaction between C2S and CaO, and the stronger diffraction intensity of CaTiO3 with the doping addition of CaF2 and TiO2 increasing also indicated that the addition of CaF2 would be adverse to the solution of TiO2 in the doped C3S.

In Table 3, It could be noticed that the pure C3S had the lowest symmetry with triclinic form T3, three characteristic peaks were detected between 31.5° and 33°, three characteristic peaks were detected between 51° and 52.5°, and the last two peaks between 51° and 52.5° had a tendency to merge [43]. The doped C3S with 1.0% CaF2 was determined as the polymorph coexistence of T3 and M1, the main phase could be identified as M1-type C3S [41–42]. The doped C3S with 1.0% CaF2 and 0.5% TiO2 had the same feature as sample F1, but the characteristic peaks between 51° and 52.5° was more close the T3-type C3S [43]. It might mean that the doping addition of 1.0% CaF2 and 0.5% TiO2 would lower the symmetry of C3S. The doped C3S with 1.0% CaF2 and 1.0% TiO2 presented the M1-type C3S, and the doped C3S with 1.0% CaF2 and 2.0% TiO2 presented the M3-type C3S [42,46].

The doped C3S with 1.5% CaF2 presented the polymorph coexistence of T3 and M1, the main phase would be identified as M1-type C3S, and the feature of T3-type C3S nearly disappeared. Although the doped C3S with 1.5% CaF2 and 0.5% TiO2 also showed the polymorph coexistence of T3 and M1, the characteristic peaks between 51° and 52.5° came to be more similar as T3-type C3S than sample F2. The relative low addition of TiO2 (<0.5%) might disorganize the formation of C3S polymorphs doped with CaF2 to make the structure characteristics of T3-type C3S more measurable, in other words, the relative low addition of TiO2 might promote the presence of the superstructure of T3-type C3S along with the reduction in polymorph symmetry [47]. The doped C3S with 1.5% CaF2 and 1.0% TiO2 showed the M3-type C3S. The characteristic peaks between 31.5° and 33° of the doped C3S with 1.5% CaF2 and 2.0% TiO2 came to merge to two peaks, it was pivotal to identify the R-type C3S [36,43], and the peaks between 51° and 52.5° showed M3-type C3S, it exhibited the polymorph coexistence of R and M3.

The doped C3S with 2.0% CaF2 came to present M3-type C3S, and the doped C3S with 2.0% CaF2 and 0.5% TiO2 showed the same polymorphs as sample F2T2. The C3S polymorphs with the addition of 2.0% CaF2 and 0.5% TiO2 was different from the doped C3S with 1.0% or 1.5% CaF2, it could be found that the doping addition of 0.5% TiO2 and 2.0% CaF2 was useful to promote the transformation from low symmetry polymorph to high symmetry polymorph of C3S. Both Sample F3T1 and F3T2 had the typical features of R-type C3S: two characteristic peaks were between 31.5° and 33° and one characteristic peak was between 51° and 52.5°.

It could be concluded that the addition of CaF2 from 1.0% to 2.0% was beneficial to elevate the symmetry of C3S polymorph compared with the undoped C3S, while the co-doping addition of CaF2 and TiO2 would increase the complexity of C3S polymorphs. Incorporating 0.5% TiO2 into the doped C3S with 1.0% or 1.5% CaF2 would reduce the symmetry of C3S polymorph to some extent. It could be noticed that the co-doping of CaF2 and TiO2 had the more positive influence on the symmetry of C3S polymorphs compared with that doped with CaF2.

ce:section.ce:section-title: IR spectra analysis of doped C3S samples
ce:section.ce:para: The various C3S polymorphs were very similar to each other in terms of the atomic site occupation of the calcium cation, oxygen ion and silicon cation, only the orientation of [SiO4]4− tetrahedra presented some differences [40]. The IR absorption bands of the doped C3S sample in the range of 400–1400 cm−1 could be mainly caused by the vibration of [SiO4]4− tetrahedron, and the isolated [SiO4]4− tetrahedra consisted of four vibration modes, including symmetric stretching vibration (ν1), asymmetric stretching vibration (ν3), in-plane bending vibration (ν2) and out-plane bending vibration (ν4) [43].

Fig. 2 (a–c) provided the IR spectra of different doped C3S, and the information of various vibration bands were listed in Table 4 . The main vibrations of the undoped C3S sample had no symmetric stretching vibration (ν1), but had the asymmetric stretching vibration (ν3) at 937 and 890 cm−1, in-plane bending vibration (ν2) at 454 cm−1 and out-plane bending vibration (ν4) at 524 cm−1, it could imply that the polymorph of undoped C3S would be a T3-type C3S. This result was also demonstrated by Ren, De la Torre and Peterson that the sharp symmetric stretching vibration of T3-type C3S at approximately 812 cm−1 would vanish differing from T1-type or T2-type C3S [43,48,49]. The main vibrations of sample F1 and F1T0 were similar, only some small shifts of the in-plane bending and asymmetric stretching vibration could be observed. But sample F1T2 showed a distinct change at 751 and 728 cm−1 symmetric stretching vibration, it was corresponding to the characteristic vibration of Metal-Oxygen (M−O) bond [50], and the presence of CaTiO3 just indicated the existence of Ti-O bond. The asymmetric stretching vibration at 751 and 728 cm−1 could conform to the characteristic of Ti-O vibrational mode as well [51].

The vibration modes of the doped system with 1.5% CaF2 were similar to that with 1.0% CaF2, the symmetric stretching vibration of sample F2T2 also confirmed the existence of Ti-O bond. The formation of CaTiO3 and β-C2S could be a concomitant process analyzed by Section 3.1, the characteristic IR spectra of β-C2S in sample F1T2 and F2T2 was not observed, and it might be due to the interference of the phase contents and sample sampling. The vibration modes of the doped system with 2.0% CaF2 were similar to that with 1.5% CaF2, but the asymmetric stretching vibration at 751 and 846 cm−1 was different, the asymmetric stretching vibration at 846 cm−1 was corresponding to a characteristic vibration spectra of β-C2S [51].

It could be found that there were only minor changes in the IR spectra of all the doped C3S samples due to the fact that the IR spectra of higher symmetry polymorphs M1, M3 and R are similar to that of T3 [43]. Meanwhile, IR spectra of sample Control, F1T2, F2T2 and F3T2 were observed that the characteristic peaks for the polymorphs (T3, M3, R + M3, R) became broader with the increase of the polymorph symmetry of C3S, it was also reported by Ren [43]. In addition, the asymmetric stretching vibration of sample Control, F1T2, F2T2 and F3T2 presented a consistent shift to lower wave numbers, it might be originated from the increase of the polymorph symmetry of C3S. However, to understand the effect of CaF2 and TiO2 on the atomic site occupation of the structure of C3S, the more in-depth researches still need to be put forward.

ce:section.ce:section-title: XPS analysis of doped C3S samples
ce:section.ce:para: XPS would provide the binding energies (BE) of the core-level electronic states of the elements in the surface region, and the valuable information concerning the elements could effectively explain the binding situation of key elements [52]. To explore the chemical valence states of fluorine and titanium in the doped C3S, the binding energies of fluorine and titanium were investigated by XPS narrow spectrum using Gaussian Fitting method. Fig. 3 (a–b) showed XPS survey spectrum and narrow spectrum of F1s for the doped C3S with 2.0% CaF2. Fig. 4 (a–c) showed XPS survey spectrum, F1s narrow spectrum and Ti2p narrow spectrum for the doped C3S with 2.0% CaF2 and 2.0% TiO2.

In Fig. 3 (a), the major surface components were Ca, Si, C (due to the C pollution), O and F. Fig. 3 (b) showed the only one Gaussian Fitting peak of F1s at 685.05 eV, it was corresponding to the F− of CaF2 according to the spectra retrieval [39]. The absence of CaF2 in the doped C3S with 2.0% CaF2 hinted the solution of F in the structure of C3S, and the F− would replace some O2− to bind Ca2+. The replacement of O2− by F− would cause an excess of positive charge, it would be made up by the calcium vacancies [29–30]. The defect reaction:

In Fig. 4 (a), the major surface components were Ca, Si, C (due to the C pollution) and O, the components of F and Ti were relatively minor due to the sintering uniformity and detection depth limit of XPS. The XPS narrow spectrum of F1s and Ti2p also could give necessary information by Gaussian Fitting. Fig. 4 (b) presented one main Gaussian Fitting peak of F1s at 684.63 eV, it was also corresponding to the F− of CaF2 according to the spectra retrieval [39]. The finding indicated that in the doped C3S with CaF2 and TiO2, the binding situation of fluorine would not be interfered by the addition of TiO2. Fig. 4 (c) presented two main Gaussian Fitting peak at 458.18 eV (Ti2p 3/2) and 463.39 eV (Ti2p 1/2), the Ti2p 3/2 peak at 458.18 eV was corresponding to the Ti-O of CaTiO3 using the spectra retrieval [39], and the Ti2p 1/2 peak at 463.39 eV was corresponding to the Ti-O of TiO2 using the spectra retrieval [39]. It could be noticed that the Ti-O of CaTiO3 would be consistent with the XRD analysis, and another Ti-O of TiO2 could be an evidence of titanium solution in the structure of C3S. The Ti4+ could substitute Si4+ of [SiO4]4− tetrahedra, and the substitution of Si4+ by Ti4+ would keep the charge balance, the finding could be verified by several researches [30,36]. ce:section.ce:section-title: Hydration heat evolution of doped C3S samples
ce:section.ce:para: The induction period of the doped C3S was prolonged obviously compared with the undoped C3S, and the induction period of the doped C3S with 2.0% CaF2 and 2.0% TiO2 was prolonged to approximately 40 h, it might mainly result from the formation of low cementitious CaTiO3 and β-C2S [37]. The appearing time of acceleration period from early to last would be: Control, F1, F2, F2T0, F3 and F3T2. The heat flow of the acceleration period were evidently slowed down, as a result, the main formation process of C-S-H gel would be retarded, and the incorporation of TiO2 into the doped C3S with CaF2 would aggravate the retardation of the hydration in the acceleration period. The retardation mechanism was once revealed by the hypothesis that special foreign ions would generate a least soluble barrier layers, it could precipitate onto the surface of hydrated C3S to retard the further hydration [33,57]. The total hydration heat of the doped C3S in Fig. 6 also characterized the positive effect of the addition of CaF2 and TiO2 on the initial hydration of C3S, but the negative effect on the later periods. It could be found that the dopant types displayed the more obvious effect than the types of C3S polymorphs on the hydration activity of C3S. However, more investigations should be carried out to prove the validity of above hypothesis or other retardation mechanism of the obtained findings.

The conclusions might be drawn from the present research as follows:
1.
A certain addition of CaF2 would accelerate the appearance of the solution limit of TiO2 to generate CaTiO3 in the doped C3S. The formation of CaTiO3 and β-C2S was a concomitant process as the solution limit of TiO2 reached.
2.
The pure C3S had the lowest symmetry with a triclinic form T3, and the addition of TiO2 and CaF2 would make the transformation process of polymorph complicated. The addition of 0.5% TiO2 and the addition of 1.0% or 1.5% CaF2 would lead to the reduction of C3S polymorph symmetry, however more addition of CaF2 and TiO2 could actualize the change to the higher polymorph symmetry of C3S. The co-doping addition of CaF2 and TiO2 generally could promote the polymorphic transformation of C3S from low symmetry to higher symmetry.
3.
There were only minor changes in the IR spectra of the different doped C3S samples, and the IR spectra of the selected samples with different polymorphs (T3, M3, R + M3, R) were observed that the characteristic peaks for the polymorphs became broader with the increase of the polymorph symmetry of doped C3S.
4.
In the doped C3S, the binding situation of fluorine would not be interfered by the introduction of titanium. The appearance of Ti2p 1/2 peak at 463.39 eV proved the solution of titanium in the structure of C3S, and the defect reaction of could be regarded as:

5.
The doped C3S showed a higher heat flow than the undoped C3S in the initial period, but the increased addition of CaF2 presented a negative effect on the initial hydration of C3S. The addition of TiO2 weakened the above effect, and more addition of TiO2 would present more rapid initial hydration rate. However, the heat flow of the doped C3S in the acceleration period was evidently slowed down, and the incorporation of TiO2 into the doped C3S would aggravate the retardation effect caused by CaF2 in the acceleration period. The results from hydration heat evolution revealed that the dopant types show a more distinct effect than the types of C3S polymorph on the hydration activity of C3S.
